pĕcūnĭāris , e, adj. pecunia,
I.of or belonging to money, pecuniary (post-class. and rare for pecuniarius): “damnatio,” i. e. to pay a fine, Dig. 48, 19, 10 fin. dub. (al. pecuniaria).—Hence, adv.: pĕcūnĭārĭter , relating to money, pecuniarily, Dig. 47, 1, 3.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
